page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-48 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical Intel Xeon processor cores running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The hardware configuration allocates 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test registers a score of 44,617.16, while the single-core score is 1,410.49. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 2,446.02 GB/sec, which drops to 153.47 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 79.98 GB/sec. In application-specific benchmarks, the instance achieves 41.27 million operations per second on Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 29.33 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the weak category at 23.8 GB/sec, and LLM text generation for a small 135M model is also weak at 53.69 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highcpu-48 offers a high density of dedicated compute cores relative to memory, making it a viable option for CPU-bound workloads where large memory footprints are not required. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs means users only pay for raw CPU and memory capacity. This profile is suited for multi-threaded processing tasks, software compilation, ray tracing, and high-throughput web serving.
